title: dfilter: Make string slices a return an FT_STRING
description:
Allow string slices (indexing) to work with internationalized
strings. The old behavior of indexing on byte boundaries can
be obtained using raw slices.

@@ -322,11 +322,10 @@ Otherwise date and time values are interpreted as local time.
 
 === The slice operator
 
-You can take a slice of a field if the field is a text string or a
-byte array.
-For example, you can filter on
-the vendor portion of an ethernet address (the first three bytes) like
-this:
+You can take a slice of a field if the field base type is a text string or a
+byte array (the base type of most network address fields is bytes).
+For example, you can filter on the vendor portion of an ethernet address
+(the first three bytes) like this:
 
     eth.src[0:3] == 00:00:83
 
@@ -350,6 +349,7 @@ The following syntax governs slices:
     [:j]     start_offset = 0, length = j
     [i:]     start_offset = i, end_offset = end_of_field
 
+Slice indexes are zero-based.
 Offsets can be negative, in which case they indicate the
 offset from the *end* of the field.  The last byte of the field is at offset
 -1, the last but one byte is at offset -2, and so on.
@@ -361,6 +361,21 @@ or
 
     frame[-4:] == 0.1.2.3
 
+As mentioned above the slice operator can be used on string and byte fields
+and will respectively produce string or byte slices. String slices are
+indexed on UTF-8 codepoint boundaries (i.e: internationalized characters),
+so the following comparison is true:
+
+    "touché"[5] == "é"
+
+The example above generates an error because the compiler rejects constant
+expressions but is otherwise syntactically correct and examplifies the
+behaviour of string slices.
+
+To obtain a byte slice of the same string the raw (@) operator can be used:
+
+    @"touché"[5-6] == c3:a9
+
 A slice can always be compared against either a string or a byte sequence.
 
 Slices can be combined. You can concatenate them using the comma operator:

+  ** Using the slice operator with strings produces a string. Previously it

commits_data.title: dfilter: Make string slices a return an FT_STRING
commits_data.message:
dfilter: Make string slices a return an FT_STRING

Allow string slices (indexing) to work with internationalized
strings. The old behavior of indexing on byte boundaries can
be obtained using raw slices.

commits_data.title: Data: Add text as UTF-8 instead of ASCII
commits_data.message:
Data: Add text as UTF-8 instead of ASCII

Allow the use of UTF-8 as text payload for the data dissector.

This is a quase-generated field without any sort of standard so use
UTF-8 instead. It's more useful and general.

commits_data.title: Compute slice ranges in a separate procedure
commits_data.message:
Compute slice ranges in a separate procedure

Modularize the code to allow re-use.

commits_data.title: dfilter: Fix raw slices
commits_data.message:
dfilter: Fix raw slices

Fix raw slices to always have FT_BYTES type.

Before:

    Filter:
     @_ws.ftypes.string[3:4] == ff:ff

    Instructions:
     0000 READ_TREE        @_ws.ftypes.string <FT_STRING> -> R0
     0001 IF_FALSE_GOTO    4
     0002 SLICE            R0[3:4]          -> R1
     0003 ANY_EQ           R1 == ff:ff <FT_BYTES>
     0004 RETURN

After:

    Filter:
     @_ws.ftypes.string[3:4] == ff:ff

    Instructions:
     0000 READ_TREE        @_ws.ftypes.string <FT_BYTES> -> R0
     0001 IF_FALSE_GOTO    4
     0002 SLICE            R0[3:4]          -> R1
     0003 ANY_EQ           R1 == ff:ff <FT_BYTES>
     0004 RETURN

commits_data.title: dflter: Fix semantics of fvalue length
commits_data.message:
dflter: Fix semantics of fvalue length

Do not mix wire size, a protocol property, with fvalue
length, a property of certain types of objects (sequences).

Rename ftype_length() to ftype_wire_size(). Do not return
wire_size with fvalue_length() (use ftype_wire_size()
instead).

Make the semantic check reject taking the len() of objects
that are not arrays or lists. If the (fixed) len() of a number
is somehow useful we can add a different function for that.
